world.h: Iran threatens to 'rain down hell' if US escalates war
world.b: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned the US against escalation. President Trump said renewed strikes are "highly unlikely" if talks on Iran's nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz progress.
world.title: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war

world.h: Europe to join US-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
world.b: France's foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, said European officials will attend this week's Russia-Ukraine talks in the UAE despite Kremlin objections. The meetings are set for Tuesday and Wednesday.
world.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections

world.h: US launches task force to cut Iran's land supply routes
world.b: CENTCOM's new Task Force Iron Gate, based in Tampa, will work to stop weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue from crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Commander Adm. Brad Cooper said it will reinforce the US blockade at sea.

world.h: Drone hits Iraqi Kurdish gasfield as blasts heard in Iran's Qeshm
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage of the US-Israel war on Iran.
world.title: Drone hits Iraq Kurdish region gasfield, blasts in Iran’s Qeshm

national.h: Floods give Southwest reservoirs rare relief as Lake Powell rises 20 feet
national.b: Storms in late October and early November forced evacuations but are refilling lakes and aquifers that had fallen to record lows during a yearslong megadrought.

national.h: Texas ER didn't give bleeding newborn a vitamin K shot for hours, ProPublica reports
national.b: Eleven-day-old Gwen Biesenbach, whose parents chose vitamin K drops instead of the standard injection, bled from her belly button as an ER doctor tried seven methods to stop it. The family has filed a complaint with the Texas Medical Board.
national.title: An 11-Day-Old Baby Couldn’t Stop Bleeding. For Hours, the ER Didn’t Provide a Critical Vitamin Shot.

politics.h: Native American women made history in this week's elections
politics.b: Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the Senate, Deb Haaland the first to win a governorship, and Crystalyne Curley the first woman elected president of the Navajo Nation.
politics.title: Native American women made history in tribal, state and federal elections

politics.h: Midterms energized abuse survivors as a political force
politics.b: In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton won the governor's race by 8 points after Vivek Ramaswamy spent $4 million on an ad questioning her account of childhood abuse, which court records confirmed. Survivors told The 19th the ad pushed them to get involved.
politics.title: The midterms energized a powerful political constituency: abuse survivors

politics.h: Staff at US AI safety center told to report to the White House, AP sources say
politics.b: The Commerce Department division that assesses new AI systems lacks a permanent leader and has stopped publishing its research, according to two former officials.
politics.title: AP sources: Staff at U.S. center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns

politics.h: Gen Z voters helped fuel the Democratic wave
politics.b: Exit polls show Democrats carried voters under 30 by nearly 50 points on Tuesday, a sharp shift from 2024. In Texas, James Talarico won his Senate race by 12 points overall and by 60 among Gen Z.
politics.title: How Gen Z voters helped fuel a blue wave for Democrats

international.h: Pope Leo arrives in Argentina and tells Milei people must come first
international.b: In his first speech in Buenos Aires, Leo said "the economy must serve the person, not the person the economy," a subtle critique of President Javier Milei's austerity agenda.
international.title: Pope Leo arrives in Argentina and tells Milei that people, not the economy, should come first

international.h: Hundreds of thousands march in Amsterdam against ties with Israel
international.b: 'Red Line' protesters packed Museum Square to condemn the Dutch government's economic and military ties with Israel and to call for a halt to arms sales.
international.title: Hundreds of thousands join Amsterdam’s ‘Red Line’ protest against Israel

international.h: Train collision near Cairo kills 7 and injures more than 100
international.b: A train bound for Fayoum crashed into the rear of a stationary Aswan-bound train in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo. The conductor was among the dead.

international.h: Russian strikes leave hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power
international.b: An overnight attack on an energy facility cut electricity in Dnipro and surrounding districts, and another 250,000 people lost power in the Kharkiv region. DTEK said repeated attacks are complicating repairs.

international.h: South Africa's ANC slips to 31% in local elections
international.b: With 99% of votes counted, the ANC trails its 2021 result by about 14 points, ahead of the Democratic Alliance at 25%. Jacob Zuma's uMkhonto weSizwe party is third with about 10%.

international.h: Floods in Gaza leave tens of thousands without shelter
international.b: Heavy rain and strong winds tore through tents across the Gaza Strip. Al Jazeera reports nearly 400,000 displaced Palestinians are sheltering in places considered highly vulnerable to more flooding.

international.h: At least 21 dead as boat capsizes off Senegal
international.b: The pirogue overturned Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes between Dakar and Saint-Louis, and one person was rescued. The Interior Ministry called the toll provisional as the search continues.

international.h: Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers
international.b: At least 16 more were wounded at a base in Santa Rosa del Sur in northern Colombia. Authorities have not said who carried out the strike, and President Abelardo de la Espriella said those behind it "will have nowhere to hide."

international.h: Magnitude 5.7 earthquake injures more than 20 in central Japan
international.b: The quake struck at 1:04 a.m. Sunday in western Shizuoka Prefecture, shattering shop windows in Aichi and Shizuoka. No tsunami warning was issued, and the weather agency warned of possible strong quakes in the coming week.

international.h: Canary Islands' El Hierro declares emergency over migrant arrivals
international.b: More than 3,300 people have reached the island of about 11,400 residents in roughly 30 boats since the start of November. Local leaders asked Madrid for help, and the Canary Islands' regional leader called the situation "absolutely unsustainable."

business.h: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over relationship
business.b: The board opened a probe after Huang confirmed an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and Huang will keep leading Nvidia.
business.title: US chipmaker Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair

sports.h: Ja'Marr Chase leads Bengals past Falcons 34-17 in Madrid
sports.b: Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown, most of it in the first half, as Cincinnati won on international soil for the first time.
sports.title: NFL Week 9 winners and losers: Ja'Marr Chase goes ballistic, another baffling Commanders botch

sports.h: NC State finalizing deal to hire Philip Rivers as coach
sports.b: The former Wolfpack quarterback has coached high school football in Alabama since 2021, and this would be his first college job. He would replace Dave Doeren, who was fired after a Week 8 loss to Stanford.
The Irish win opens the top spot in the rankings. CBS Sports projects Georgia will reclaim No. 1 in Sunday's AP poll after a wire-to-wire win at Ole Miss, with Tennessee moving into the top 10.

sports.h: Oregon stuns Ohio State in college football's Week 10
sports.b: No. 23 Oregon won at Ohio State, and No. 3 Utah beat No. 9 BYU in the Holy War rivalry. Ohio State and LSU moved outside the playoff bubble.
LSU led 13-10 in the third quarter before Alabama scored 21 unanswered points, handing Lane Kiffin his sixth straight loss to the Crimson Tide. LSU falls to 6-3.

sports.h: Man arrested for stalking outside LeBron James' LA home
sports.b: James, now with the 76ers, was in Cleveland when the incident happened.

sports.h: Colts listening to offers for Daniel Jones
sports.b: Multiple teams have called about the quarterback ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, ESPN reports.

sports.h: Nebraska fires offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen
sports.b: Matt Rhule made the change after a 24-13 loss to Illinois dropped the Huskers to 5-4 following a 5-0 start.

sports.h: Winless Chargers to keep Khalil Mack at deadline
sports.b: The 0-7 Chargers reportedly told teams Mack stays, and gave 'hard nos' on Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

sports.h: Luka Doncic's historic start for the Lakers
sports.b: Doncic has the Lakers atop the West at 8-2, with games of 52 and 53 points so far.

goodnews.h: Chile's Atacama Desert bursts into its biggest bloom in decades
goodnews.b: Record El Niño rains turned the world's driest non-polar desert into fields of pink, yellow and purple wildflowers.
goodnews.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades

local.h: New York sends 20 Democrats and 6 Republicans to the House
local.b: Democrat Cait Conley flipped the Hudson Valley's 17th District by defeating Rep. Mike Lawler. Rep. Nicole Malliotakis remains the city's only Republican in Congress.
local.title: New York’s House delegation will include 20 Democrats and six Republicans

local.h: Woman dies after falling from moving SUV on the BQE
local.b: Police said the 37-year-old opened a rear door and fell out near the Brooklyn Bridge around 2:30 a.m. Sunday, then was struck by another car. No arrests have been made.
local.title: Brooklyn woman killed after tumbling from a moving SUV on the BQE near Brooklyn Bridge

periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 51. West wind around 14 mph.

periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 59. Northwest wind 15 to 18 mph, with gusts as high as 29 mph.

periods.text: Partly cloudy, with a low around 48. Northwest wind 10 to 14 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Partly sunny, then gradually becoming sunny, with a high near 61. West wind 9 to 14 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. West wind around 10 mph.

localgood.h: Brooklyn jogger killed in stabbing saves four lives through organ donation
localgood.b: LiveOnNY said Katie Suarez's heart, liver, pancreas and kidneys went to four recipients ages 12 to 75.
localgood.title: Brooklyn jogger killed in stabbing saves 4 lives through organ donations

localgood.h: Mamdani expands free produce programs for SNAP recipients
localgood.b: The city is adding funding to Health Bucks and Get the Good Stuff, which matches SNAP spending on fresh or frozen fruits, vegetables and beans dollar for dollar.
localgood.title: Mamdani expands free produce programs for New Yorkers on SNAP
